public_rationale: DayDreamer demonstrated useful physical-world learning before the post. Its robots learned through interaction and world models, including learning locomotion from scratch, without needing a corpus of people's personal information. That contradicts the ordinary task-level reading of the existence claim. The result depends on that reading: the paper does not establish a general-purpose replacement for the whole prevailing AI paradigm.
limitations: The result turns on the unspecified breadth of effective in the world.
The evidence is an author-reported research demonstration, not an independent replication.
The demonstrations establish bounded capabilities rather than general intelligence.

statement.excerpt: One can imagine an alternative AI paradigm that could learn much of what it needed to know to be effective in the world without going through all your personal data, but that does not yet exist.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that no demonstrated learning approach could acquire useful real-world capabilities without extensive access to people's personal information.
Effective means demonstrated competence on real-world tasks. The statement does not explicitly require human-level general intelligence.
An alternative can be a different learning approach, such as learning through interaction and an internal world model; it need not abandon neural networks.
The existence claim covers research demonstrated by September 7, 2023. Its cumulative target period has no stated starting date.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishing that approaches demonstrated by the post date could not learn useful real-world capabilities without extensive personal-data collection.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A demonstrated learning approach available by the post date that acquired useful real-world capabilities from interaction or other sources without extensive personal-data collection.

evidence.explanation: By this date, the authors had publicly reported a world-model learning approach demonstrated on four physical robots, including locomotion, manipulation, and navigation. Learning from direct interaction and from scratch provides a counterexample under the stated reading; the inference concerns these demonstrated tasks, not unrestricted intelligence.
